_prereg: PAN-37 part 2: seeded-bug calibration set for agent-run code reviews, frozen 2026-10-10 BEFORE generation.
Purpose: measure how often a reviewer (an agent or a model) finds a real bug and how often it raises a false
alarm, so review findings can be weighted by measured reliability instead of trusted. The set is built from the
PAN-34 primary tasks (functions of the program whose own test file sees them), so every seeded bug is one the
program's tests detect: a 'known bug' with ground truth.
source: the 142 PAN-34 primary tasks (manifest 46e2343aa, amendment A2), their sandbox and worker copies

operators.cmp_flip: one comparison operator swapped: < <-> <=, > <-> >=, == <-> !=, in <-> not in, is <-> is not

mutation_rule: the mutated expression's source segment is replaced by the unparsed mutated expression; every other character of the module is unchanged (no reformatting tells)
selection: tasks shuffled with random.Random(37); per task one site drawn with the same generator from all applicable sites; a mutant is KEPT only if its task's test file FAILS with it (killed); stop at 40 kept mutants; then 20 CLEAN items (unmutated functions) from tasks not used for mutants, same generator
secrecy: items (the code a reviewer sees) and the answer key (mutated line, operator, original and mutated segment) are written to the M2 lake only (C:/Prometheus-data/pan/lake/reviewcal/), never to the repository or the database; their sha256 are committed so the key can be checked when revealed

scoring.hit: on a mutant item, a finding that cites a line within +-2 of the mutated line
scoring.miss: a mutant item with no hit
scoring.false_alarm: a clean item with any finding claiming a bug
scoring.metrics: recall = hits / 40 and false-alarm rate = false alarms / 20, each with a Wilson 95 percent interval; a reviewer whose recall interval lies below 0.5 is reported as unreliable for unsupervised review

amendments.change: CHANNEL found on inspection: every item's unmutated original is in the repository, so a reviewer with repository (or pan search) access can find a seeded bug by diffing instead of reviewing. Calibration scores are therefore valid ONLY for reviewers run WITHOUT repository access (prompt-only: the item's code, optionally its module context from the sandbox). Packets handed to reviewers omit module path, task id and line numbers in the module; the items file in the lake keeps them for scoring.
amendments.evidence: items file ITEMS_20261010T072739Z.json carries module/start/end/task_id (needed for scoring)

amendments.change: Bookkeeping: the generator's 'survivors' was candidates tried minus mutants kept -- an upper bound, because the last batch's extra killed mutants were not needed. The counter now counts mutants the tests did NOT catch. First set: 64 tried, 40 kept, survivors <= 24.

CHANCE FLOORS + SET v1 UNFIT. What a reviewer scores WITHOUT reviewing, under the frozen rule (python -m pan reviewcal floors; aggregates only): random line 0.379 recall at false-alarm 1.0; middle line 0.40; the line whose +-2 window holds most sites of the published operators 0.525 [0.375, 0.671]; a regex for the operators' textual signatures (`return None` from return_none, `not (` from ast.unparse in negate_if; flag that line, else abstain) 0.45 [0.307, 0.602] at false-alarm 0.05 (1/20); regex else site density 0.80 [0.652, 0.895] at 1.0. The frozen reliability rule (recall interval upper bound < 0.5 => unreliable) passes every one of these non-reviewers. Consequences: (1) set v1 (ITEMS_20261010T072739Z) is NOT used to calibrate any reviewer -- it measures pattern-spotting: 21 of 40 mutants carry their operator's text signature (return None: 14/40 mutant items, 0/20 clean; `not (`: 12/40 mutant, 1/20 clean); (2) a successor set v2 (backlog PAN-39) must pass a tell gate before freezing; (3) any reviewer is reported against the floors and counts as better than chance only if its recall exceeds the strongest floor scaled to its own false-alarm rate (abstaining at random moves a floor along recall = R_floor x FA).
